extracted.intended_audience: communications, public relations, and marketing professionals (PR practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting press releases that attract attention from journalists, search engines, and stakeholders by optimizing headline, length, lead, and distribution timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: relevance and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: The headline should be relevant and concise as it is the first thing readers and search engines look at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the headline focused on the most important point; make it immediately relevant to the audience. Avoid vague or long-winded headlines — the headline is a primary element both for human readers and for search engine scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline length and keyword placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit headline character length to 88 characters or less and put the most important keywords within the first 55–70 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific character limits improve readability and search discoverability. Prioritize the key phrase or words at the very start of the headline so search engines and quick-scanning readers see them first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with 'why' (front-load your key message)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the press release by answering 'why' — why should your audience care?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the most important message so readers get the main point quickly. This helps ensure key messages are communicated even if the reader does not finish the whole release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length / conciseness: target ~600 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep press releases around 600 words because longer releases are less likely to be read in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter, focused releases increase the chance that recipients will read the whole piece and absorb the key messages. Use concision to prioritize essential facts and the 'why' up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: avoid peak send times to stand out
rubrics_metrics.description: Send releases at off times rather than the common on-the-hour or half-hour bursts (52% of news is sent on the hour and half hour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-volume send times (e.g., Tuesdays at 8:00 AM ET) create noise; sending at atypical times (example: 8:47 AM ET) can help a release stand out to journalists and editors.
